answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. Written in a numbers heavy, no adjectives register, it stays short. The design leans on time-locked work history, clawed back after a replayed submission, duplicates are caught by replay, not by name. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the walnut of payment, so volume alone buys nothing. A reef of per-task receipts records who did what, and the grove of that record is inspected by auditors who gain nothing from passing it.
